conviction_note: The evidence nets to roughly zero: a cleaner peer read from VF (Oct 28) and a moderately crowded short work against higher oil and freight since the July guide, a strong El Nino warm-winter outlook on a Q4 that needs about +6% sales, and a promotional backdrop. abs_move 7.5 rests on the 7.34% event-implied move (indicative, spread 53% of mid) and the 5.43% median, raised because this print carries the Q4 guide and the Spring 2027 order-book update. p_up is 47 because the reaction history is 2 up of 7 and the beat on Q2 was sold (-5.43%) on a soft guide. The findings sum (-0.2) and the scaled number (-0.45) agree in sign and size.
bar: Q3 revenue ~$938-943m and EPS $1.25-1.28. Earnings Whispers has $1.25 / $938.1m, whisper $1.31 (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/COLM). Benzinga has $1.28 / ~$942.5m (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/COLM/earnings-forecasts). Company Q3 guide is net sales $929-943m (-1.5% to flat) and diluted EPS $1.15-1.35, operating margin 8.1-9.5%; FY26 guide is sales $3.43-3.50B, EPS $4.45-4.90 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001050797/000105079726000129/colmfy26q2exhibit991.htm). Consensus sits at the EPS guide midpoint and at the top of the revenue guide. Two estimate sources agree within 3 cents and the company guide exists, so the bar counts as sourced.
positioning_check: Short interest is 4,327,124 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, 6.35 days to cover, against 4,372,692 (6.28 DTC) on 09-30 and 4,281,367 (6.12) on 08-31 (https://equibles.com/stocks/colm/short-interest). That is about 8.5% of the 51.19m shares outstanding and about 13.6-13.8% of float per Benzinga in Aug/Sep (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/COLM/sentiment). The float is small because the Boyle family holds a large stake, so the short is moderately crowded and flat-to-rising into the print. 25d skew is +4.85 vol points (downside paid). Put/call OI ratio is 10.07, but total OI is only 2,259, so the options signal is thin. The stock is +10.1% over 20 days and -6.3% from its 52-week high.

findings.finding: Columbia beat its own revenue guidance and consensus in both reported 2026 quarters. Q1 revenue was $779.0m vs a $755.6m consensus, with EPS $0.65 vs $0.35. Q2 revenue was $614.4m vs ~$607m. Consensus for Q3 ($938-942.5m, EPS $1.25-1.28) sits at the top of the $929-943m revenue guide and the middle of the $1.15-1.35 EPS guide. Management said the >$30m Q3-to-Q4 shift is timing, 'not a function of any cancellations', and that there were 'no changes in our order book for fall 2026'. A modest beat on the quarter is the base case, at about +1% revenue vs bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 beat with raised op-income guide: +2.35%. Q2 2026 beat on revenue with a soft Q3 guide: -5.43%. 5 of the last 7 prints fell, so this name has not reliably paid for quarterly beats.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. The whisper ($1.31) is already above consensus, and consensus sits at the top of the revenue guide. If the market expected a large beat, the whisper would sit at or above the $1.35 top of guide. It does not.
findings.independence: Q2 beat in the Q2 exhibit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001050797/000105079726000129/colmfy26q2exhibit991.htm). The 'no cancellations / no change in fall order book' quote is from the Q2 call (https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-1949254-20260731). These are company sources, not independent ones.

findings.finding: Input costs worsened after the July guide. On the Q2 call the CFO flagged incremental outbound freight charges and fuel pressure, and cited oil 'in the $90-$100 range' as a fall 2027 headwind. Brent has held above $100 since late September ($103.50 on Oct 12), and the EIA's October outlook puts Q4 2026 Brent at $104.69. Tanker freight stays elevated after strikes near Hormuz. This raises the risk that the H2 margin guide (FY op margin 8.5-9.3%) is trimmed or that the early 2027 margin commentary is cautious.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: 'H2 outlook incrementally moderated' plus a Q3 guide below the Street gave -5.43%. Q2 2025 (2025-07-31): -12.85% on a weak outlook. Guidance cuts have been punished hard.
findings.source_date: 2026-10 (EIA October STEO; URL path undated, content refers to the Q4 2026 forecast)
findings.why_not_priced: Sell-side targets were cut after Q2 (Stifel $67, Baird $65), but the stock has since rallied 10% in 20 days to $63.5, near those targets. That rally does not look like a market discounting a margin cut from above-$100 oil. If this were priced, the stock would have drifted lower with crude from late September.
findings.independence: This is a proxy: macro-to-company transmission that the company has not confirmed since July. Brent >$100 since late Sep is in a separate source (https://www.procurementresource.com/news-and-articles/brent-crude-oil-falls-to-103-50-dollars-per-barrel). The company's own sensitivity comes from the Q2 call (https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-1949254-20260731).

findings.finding: NOAA's 2026-27 Winter Outlook (Oct 16) projects a very strong El Nino with warmer-than-average temperatures across much of the northern US for Dec-Feb. This lands on the quarter Columbia's guide leans on. The FY guide implies Q4 sales of about $1.09-1.18bn: FY $3.43-3.50bn less Q1 $779.0m, Q2 $614.4m and the Q3 guide. That is roughly +6% at the midpoint including the >$30m shifted shipments, against about 4-5% underlying per the CFO. CEO Boyle on the Q2 call: 'the weather tends to be much more impactful than almost any economic indicator.' A cautious Q4 framing or a FY sales trim is the risk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 outlook prints: 2025-10-30 -3.63% and 2025-07-31 -12.85% on weak outlooks. Feb 2026 +14.44% when the FY26 guide surprised up. The guide moves this name more than the quarter does.
findings.why_not_priced: The outlook was public on Oct 16, and the stock has risen since (+2.3% over 5 days). Retail-weather risk is not visible in the price or in the sell-side targets. Partly priced through the +4.85 downside skew.
findings.independence: This is a weather proxy, not confirmed by the company. Mid/late-October cold in the Northeast (https://weatheronthisday.com/trends/halloween-weather-forecast-2026) runs the other way for October sell-through. The Q4 arithmetic uses the company's own guide (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001050797/000105079726000129/colmfy26q2exhibit991.htm).

findings.finding: A direct outerwear peer reported on Oct 28, after Columbia last spoke. VF's The North Face grew 4% in the quarter to Sep 26, with Americas +8%. Timberland Americas grew +15%. Americas ex-Dickies grew +6% 'reflecting sustained growth across channels'. VF guided TNF Q3 (Oct-Dec) to +4% or better, said it feels 'really, really good about Q3, Q4', and built inventory +7% 'to support demand in H2'. That is evidence that US outdoor/outerwear wholesale and DTC demand held through September. It supports Columbia's guided return to US wholesale growth in H2, weighted to Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No COLM-specific history on peer reads. COLM's US business fell 4% in Q2 and 8% in H1 while TNF Americas grew 8% in H1, so Columbia has been losing share. The read-through is weaker than a like-for-like.
findings.why_not_priced: It came out one session before COLM's print, and COLM consensus ($1.25-1.28, $938-942m) has not moved off the July guide midpoint. A stale bar is the pattern that has paid. Netted: VF said part of TNF's quarter was wholesale pulled forward from its Q3. Columbia's own US business has lagged TNF all year (net of share loss).
findings.independence: The VF Q2 FY27 call transcript (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/10/28/vf-vfc-q2-2027-earnings-call-transcript/) is the same company and event, so it is one source. No independent corroboration.

findings.finding: Counterparties point to a promotional, mixed fall. Dick's (Columbia's large wholesale partner) cut its FY EPS guide to $11.00-12.00 from $13.50-14.50 in late August, citing 'increasingly promotional conditions across portions of the athletic footwear and apparel marketplace'. Deckers (Oct 22) grew UGG only +3.5%, with DTC -1.8%. Columbia's CFO already built 'continued promotions' and 'more consumer pressure' into the H2 gross-margin assumptions.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. Dick's was public two months ago, and Columbia's guide already assumes promotions. The residual is that Deckers' DTC decline (Oct 22) is newer than any COLM estimate revision.
findings.independence: Deckers Q2 FY27 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000910521/000091052126000028/deckex991pressrelease-9302.htm), a different company and source. Partly offset by VF's stronger read (finding 4).

findings.finding: This print brings the first update on Spring 2027 orders. At the Q2 call about 90% of orders were in, pointing to 'a load of mid-single-digit % growth' and low-to-mid single digit H1 2027 wholesale growth. The CFO said they 'hope for the upper end and will update in October'. It is a scheduled, new forward datapoint with no known sign, so it widens the move rather than signing it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Order-book updates came with the July print (-5.43%, where the Spring order indications were overshadowed by the Q3 guide).
findings.why_not_priced: Its direction is unknown to anyone outside the company. It is filed for scale (abs_move up), not sign.
findings.independence: The Webull summary of the same call (https://www.webull.com/news/15341695072609280) is the same document.

findings.finding: The short is moderately crowded and steady into the print. 4.33m shares short at the Oct 15 settlement (6.35 days to cover) is about 8.5% of shares outstanding and about 13.8% of float per Benzinga, flat-to-up from 4.28m on Aug 31. That gives a squeeze cushion against a merely in-line or slightly negative print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Feb 2026 +14.44% on a guide surprise was the one large up move, consistent with short covering on good news. Down moves have been -3.6% to -12.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is public, but the asymmetry it creates only shows on the print. The +4.85 downside skew shows the options market is not pricing a squeeze.
findings.independence: Benzinga short float 13.6-13.8% (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/COLM/sentiment) is a different vendor with a different float definition.

findings.finding: The roughly $15m IEEPA tariff refund held as an inventory credit at June 30 is recognised in cost of sales 'relatively ratably between Q3 and Q4', about $7.5m or $0.11 EPS in Q3. It is already inside the Q3 EPS guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's $0.93 refund benefit beat the EPS bar, yet the stock fell 5.43% on the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Priced. It is inside the company guide and on the call.
findings.independence: The Q2 call (https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-1949254-20260731) is the same company.

findings.finding: There was a management reshuffle in the brand that drives the US weakness. Peter Rauch, GM of Columbia Brand North America, moved to president of Mountain Hardwear effective Sep 28, 2026, so the North America Columbia-brand lead changed mid-season. Separately, SOREL got a new president (Joe Vernachio) on Jun 22.
findings.why_not_priced: Small. Leadership churn in the Columbia brand's North America unit matters only if the call ties it to a reset.
findings.independence: The Rauch move was seen only in a FashionUnited sidebar surfaced by search (secondary, undated). The company release was found only for SOREL.

Section 122 surcharge refunds (10% paid Feb 24 to Jul 24, 2026) are still in litigation at the Federal Circuit per secondary sources. A possible future refund for Columbia, undated.

baseline_tension: The small net negative agrees with the +4.85 downside skew and 5-of-7 down history but cuts against the +10% 20-day run-up and a moderately crowded short, so p_up sits only slightly below 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (verified fact is not a reaction; Q2's beat was sold -5.43%): reported-quarter beat finding cut from +0.5 to +0.3
Rule 5 (macro-to-company transmission is a small proxy) and 'none that paid was reasoning from weather': oil/freight cut from -1.0 to -0.7, El Nino from -0.8 to -0.6
Rule 6 (inside what the company already guided): tariff-refund inventory credit cut from +0.1 to 0.0
Rule 7 / what worked (a peer print landing after the company last spoke): VF read-through left at +0.8; short-interest cushion left at +0.5; p_up moved from 46 to 47
